title: Tool engagement pathways — eval protocol and casebank
body:
Summary:

This document defines a compact, reproducible eval protocol and an accompanying casebank for evaluating new model candidates during onboarding with respect to tool engagement behavior. The goal is to measure tool selection accuracy, argument parsing robustness, and multi-step function-call flows that are representative of our production workloads in Redwood (hosted + dedicated).

Scope and motivation:
- Focus: tool-use semantics (choose which tool to call), argument construction and serialization (arg parsing), and correctness of multi-step orchestration where multiple tool calls are chained with state passed between them.
- Why: regressions in these behaviors cause customer-visible failures (incorrect API calls, bad billing, data exfiltration risks from malformed args). We want fast, automatable checks during model onboarding and for regression gating on rollouts.
- Intended runs: local dev harness, CI (nightly), and canary gating during small-percentage rollout.

High-level protocol (3 stages):
1) Unit probes: single-turn prompts that exercise edge-case arg formats (JSON arrays, nested objects, escaped strings, different date/time formats). Expected output: single function call with validated args.
2) Disambiguation & selection: ambiguous prompts where multiple tools might apply; measure selection precision/recall vs. golden label and capture justification text when model emits natural language before calling.
3) Orchestration flows: multi-step scripted scenarios (3–6 steps) that exercise state carryover, error handling (tool failure), and corrective re-invocation.

Test matrix (priority columns):
- Category: Arg parsing | Tool selection | Multi-step flow
- Priority: P0 (must pass), P1 (important), P2 (nice-to-have)
- Data type coverage: string, number, boolean, enum, date-time, URL, file-ref, embedding id, context pointer (chat-turn ref)

Representative test cases (extracts from casebank) — NOTE: each test includes prompt, model input config, expected function name, expected args (canonicalized), tolerance, and failure modes to track.

1) Arg-parsing: nested-json-escape (P0)
Prompt: "Create a calendar event titled \"Sync: Q1\" with notes: \"Discuss \"product\" roadmap and follow-up items\". Date is 2026-03-15 10:30 PST. Set reminders 24h and 15m prior."
Expected call: calendar.create_event
Canonical args: { "title": "Sync: Q1", "notes": "Discuss \"product\" roadmap and follow-up items", "start_time": "2026-03-15T10:30:00-08:00", "reminders": ["24h", "15m"] }
Tolerance: exact JSON structure, string quoting escape correctness.
Failure modes: unescaped quotes, lost nested quotes, local timezone mis-interpretation.

2) Tool-selection: pick-most-specific (P0)
Prompt: "We need to summarize the latest quarterly report and then produce bullet action items and an email draft to execs."
Tool options: [summarizer.generate, report.analyze, email.compose]
Expected primary: report.analyze (with follow-up summarizer.generate and email.compose optionally triggered in multi-step orchestrations).
Evaluation: selection accuracy (is report.analyze chosen first?), downstream correctness if executing pipeline. Track if model chooses generic summarizer only (false negative).

3) Multi-step: booking-with-fallback (P0)
Scenario: user requests booking a meeting; first tool attempt fails with 503 from roomservice.book; system should reattempt with a fallback (alternate-room) and then confirm.
Script steps:
- Step 1: model calls roomservice.book(args) -> simulate 503 error
- Step 2: harness should present error, model should either choose roomservice.book with alternate args or call roomservice.find_alternatives then roomservice.book
- Final: confirmation message with booking id.
Metrics: success-after-retry rate, average attempts, whether model surfaces error to user.

Evaluation metrics and thresholds (suggested initial gates):
- Tool selection precision (P0 tests): >= 0.93
- Arg parsing exact-match (P0 tests): >= 0.98
- Orchestration success (complete flow end-to-end): >= 0.95
- Regression sensitivity: run baseline model each evaluation to compute delta; any drop > 1% for P0 triggers failing CI.

Golden labeling and human review process:
- Each ambiguous/complex case has a canonical golden call and a short rationale field stored with the case.
- For selection ambiguity, golden label includes acceptable alternatives with priority ranking.
- Quarterly audit: sample 200 passing tests, perform human read to ensure labels still match product semantics.

Casebank composition and generation notes:
- Sources: production incident tickets (JIRA-MLINF-###), Slack threads in #toolflow, and examples from Solutions Engineering demos.
- Synthetic augmentation: programmatic generation for numeric edge cases, timezone permutations, URL encodings, and nested markdown-in-strings.
- Negative cases: prompts intended to try to force data-exfil or escalate privileges (to validate safety layers).

Harnassing + automation details:
- Harness entrypoint: infra/harness/toolflow_runner --model $MODEL --casebank cases.json --timeout 30s --seed 42
- Execution modes: dry-run (no actual external calls; simulation of tool responses), live-run (in staging with safe-mocks), canary-run (limited traffic in dedicated infra).
- Mocking rules: every external tool has a deterministic simulator with configurable latencies and error modes. For live-run, we default to read-only mocks unless a customer-signed test perm is present.
- Output artifacts: per-test JSON with fields {test_id, model, seed, observed_calls, returned_outputs, canonical_match, score, logs, err_mode}. (In storage this is a flat JSONL; here we log summary to the test dashboard.)

Scoring rubric (how we derive the single score used for gating):
- For each test: base = 1.0
- Deduct 0.5 for wrong tool selection, 0.3 for argument schema mismatch, 0.2 for mis-ordered steps in multi-step flows, 0.1 for minor serialization differences (e.g., date formatting if still parseable).
- Final model score = weighted average across all tests (P0 weight 5x, P1 weight 2x, P2 weight 1x).
- Gate: final score >= 0.95 to pass onboarding smoke.

Failure tracking and triage labels:
- Labels to attach to failing tests: selection-bias, arg-escape, timezone-wrong, missing-field, duplicate-calls, early-termination, hallucinated-tool, tolerance-break.
- Each failure should produce minimal reproducible prompt plus seed and model config and be triaged within 3 business days.

Regression-specific considerations:
- Keep baseline model snapshot artifacts in artifact-store with commit hash and model card link. Compare token-level distributions to detect subtle policy drift (e.g., sudden increase in pre-call LM justification text).
- Track latency and token-efficiency of orchestration: number of tokens spent generating intermediary conversational text vs. direct function call. If median extra tokens > 12 per flow, flag for optimization.

Privacy and safety hooks:
- Tests that would cause PII leakage are run only in dry-run with anonymized inputs. Any model that attempts to call sensitive-tool.* with non-anonymized args must fail.
- Tool selection gating: models must respect tool-level access metadata (some tools are internal-only). Add automated access check in harness.

Quick onboarding checklist for a new model candidate:
- [ ] Run unit arg-parsing probes (P0) locally, confirm >= 0.98 on arg exact-match
- [ ] Run disambiguation set against golden labels (P0) and review mismatch samples
- [ ] Execute 50 multi-step flows in dry-run, verify recovery behaviors
- [ ] Collect token-efficiency metrics and compare to baseline
- [ ] Upload artifacts and create PR linking GH-PR-4512 for review

Example of an ambiguous prompt and acceptable canonicalizations (for human reviewers):
Prompt: "Schedule prep with the product team next week and send a note to stakeholders."
Acceptable flows (ranked):
1) calendar.find_slot -> calendar.create_event -> email.compose (P0)
2) calendar.create_event with tentative flag + email.compose (P1)
3) Only email.compose with scheduling suggestion (P2)
Rationale: product workflows normally require a calendar event followed by stakeholder notification; email-only flow loses meeting metadata.

Artifacts to deliver from onboarding run:
- Full casebank used (cases.json)
- Raw run logs and per-test JSONL (compressed)
- Summary dashboard (CSV) with metrics described above
- Top 25 failing traces with contextualized prompts for SRE/Applied ML follow-up

Next steps / open questions:
- Decide final numeric gates for P1 and P2 — suggested: P1 >= 0.90, P2 >= 0.85.
- Integrate with Redwood Console rollout pipelines so a model failing P0 auto-blocks canary percent increase.
- Add fuzz-based generation of nested-escape cases (Diego) — ticket JIRA-MLINF-812 assigned.

Appendix: sample harness command and a minimal test case (executable)
- Minimal casebank snippet (single-line JSONL in harness):
  { "test_id": "arg-nested-001", "prompt": "Create an event titled \"Sync: Q1\" with notes: \"Discuss \\\"product\\\" roadmap\"", "expected_fn": "calendar.create_event", "expected_args": "{\"title\":\"Sync: Q1\",... }" }
- Run: infra/harness/toolflow_runner --model redwood-v2-small --casebank cases.jsonl --mode dry-run

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally schema-first; we expect the casebank to evolve after 2 onboarding cycles. Keep new failure tags sparse and canonical.
- Please attach any missing customer examples from Solutions Eng when doing the quarterly audit.

Document history:
- 2025-11-12: initial draft by Aisha
- 2025-12-04: added scoring rubric and harness commands (Martin)
- 2026-01-21: added canary integration notes and privacy hooks (Priya)
- 2026-02-07: added final thresholds and shifted P0 cases to stricter exact-match rules
